EQUIPMENT REQUIRED
When you were very young, you first learned how to count. Chances are, you used your fingers to keep track.
INTRODUCTIONM
You then learned how to add, subtract, multiply and divide numbers.
You use the decimal number system every day to perform tasks such as keeping track of money.s
Microprocessors use a different method for numbering. The decimal system you use is like a foreign language to them.
A microprocessor has to have numbers translated into language it can understand. A microprocessor uses "binary".
Let's begin the lesson on MICROPROCESSOR NUMBER SYSTEMS.....................
LESSON MENU
Microprocessors process data in binary form. This means they use only two symbols, 1 and 0.=
DISCUSSION
Microprocessors use binary because the 1's and 0's easily represent ON (high voltage) and OFF (low voltage).).).
To understand how a microprocessor operates, you must be familiar with the binary and hexadecimal numbering systems.
The binary numbering system is a positional system similar to our decimal system. The only difference between the two systems is the base or radix.
Base or radix means the number of symbols used. The decimal system is base 10, using ten characters. The binary system is base 2, using two characters.
These systems use only numerals, but other systems, such as hexadecimal can use a combination of characters and numerals as their symbols.
To determine what numbering system is being used, a subscript is written at the end of the number. The subscript shows the base of the numbering system.
Often the subscript is left off when it is obvious what system is being used.
In decimal, the left most digit of a quantity has the largest value and is called the Most Significant Digit (MSD).
In binary, the left most digit of a quantity also holds the largest value, but it is called the Most Significant Bit (MSB).
Similarly, the right most digit of a quantity is the smallest value and is called the Least Significant Digit (LSD) in decimal.
The character with the least value in a binary number is called LSB for the Least Significant Bit.
Each positional value is equal to the base raised by an exponent power.
For example, the first position left of the decimal point has a weight of 10 or 1 in decimal.
In binary the same position (20 ) also has a weight of 1.
Notice the change in weights when the exponent is changed.

Working with large groups of 0's and 1's is extremely difficult and unmanageable. So, the hexadecimal numbering system or "hex" was devised.
The hex system is used only to represent the binary system so that large cumbersome numbers are not necessary.
It might appear that we input hex directly to the computer, but don't forget the input device converts this input to binary.q
The hex system breaks the binary number into groups of 4 bits or nibbles. A nibble (4 bits) may be any of 16 combinations.

The combinations are represented by the hex symbol. The binary system is the most natural system for microprocessors. But the decimal system is deeply ingrained into people.
GASOLINE

Incoming data to a microprocessor is commonly in decimal form because binary is often cumbersome for many people. To make things a little easier, a different numbering system was invented, Binary Coded Decimal or BCD...
The BCD code uses a 4 bit binary structure for each decimal digit. This system is very convenient because the data input and output can be in decimal.
The only drawback is that more memory is needed to store BCD data than binary data.

Binary Multiplication - Multiplication is just a series of repeated additions.
Step 1 - To get the first partial multiplication and the LSB to the bottom with each bit of the top number, place the result under this bit.
Step 2 - To get the next partial multiplication and the next LSB to the bottom number with each bit of the top number, place the result under this number.
Step 3 - To get all partial multiplications, repeat step 2 until all bits in the bottom number (101) have been used.
Step 5 - To get the answer, add the multiplication subresults.
Last let's look at division................................
Binary Division - Division is a series of subtractions.....
Step 1 - Subtract the divisor from the dividend, starting at the MSB of the dividend.
Step 2 - Bring down the next digit from the dividend and subtract the divisor again.
Step 3 - Again, bring down the next dividend digit and subtract the divisor.
